title: Best Intercom Alternatives
intro: Fin's resolution quality gets real praise across Intercom's 2,900+ G2 reviews, but the pricing structure is the actual reason people go looking elsewhere: a $29/seat/mo Essential plan looks affordable right up until the $0.99-per-resolution fee attaches to every AI-handled conversation, and that two-part seat-plus-resolution model is the single most-cited complaint in independent reviews because it makes total monthly cost genuinely hard to forecast. Reviewers also flag Intercom as expensive relative to budget competitors like Crisp or Tidio once seat and resolution costs are combined, and a recurring gripe about thinner integration coverage than competitors offer doesn't help the value case. Two of the three picks below — Crisp and Heyy — are ones this site's author has a closer relationship with (prior contributed work for Crisp, and current growth and marketing employment at Heyy), so read those two entries as informed but not neutral; the scoring itself still runs on the same public rubric applied to every tool on this site.

entries.blurb: Zendesk is the natural next stop if what's actually bothering you about Intercom is unpredictable AI costs at scale rather than AI billing itself — it doesn't escape per-resolution charges, but it wraps them in deeper ticket routing and skills-based assignment that Intercom doesn't match. AI Agents don't unlock until the $55/agent/mo Suite Team tier (versus Intercom's Fin resolutions being billable from the $29/seat Essential plan), so the entry cost to get any AI running is actually higher on Zendesk, and Admin Copilot for human agents is gated further behind the $115/agent/mo Suite Professional tier. What you get in exchange is Zendesk's best-in-class Omnichannel Support score (5/5 in our scorecard, the top mark across every tool reviewed here) versus Intercom's already-strong 4/5, plus genuinely deeper compliance tooling — sandbox environments, custom agent roles, and approval workflows — at the Enterprise+Copilot tier. The trade-off is real: G2 data specifically flags Ease of Setup as Zendesk's weakest core metric, a documented learning curve that Intercom's more straightforward Messenger-and-inbox setup doesn't have. Pick Zendesk over Intercom if you're running a support org that needs skills-based routing and multi-channel ticket assignment more than you need Fin's specific conversational polish; stick with Intercom if a leaner team just wants AI resolution without wrestling with Zendesk's configuration depth.

Crisp is the straightforward budget move: per-workspace pricing starting at $45/mo (Mini tier, 4 seats bundled) replaces Intercom's per-seat-plus-per-resolution model entirely, and a genuinely usable free tier (2 seats, full widget and shared inbox, just no AI credits) means a small team can run real support before paying anything. Where Intercom bills $0.99 per Fin resolution on top of a $29+ seat fee, Crisp's AI automation draws down a dollar-denominated credit pool included in the plan — $25 of credits (~450 automated conversations) on the $95/mo Essentials tier, for instance — which is a more predictable cost shape even if the total automation volume is smaller. Crisp actually edges out Intercom on channel breadth in one specific way: it natively bundles Instagram DM and Facebook Messenger alongside WhatsApp, web chat, SMS, and email, while Intercom's channel list stops at chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, and phone. It gives up ground on the enterprise side, though — no equivalent to Intercom's Expert-tier SSO, HIPAA support, or multibrand messenger, and advanced features like ticketing and white-labeling are locked behind the $295/mo Plus tier. One thing worth weighing before switching: Crisp's Trustpilot score sits at a rough 1.9/5, driven by a real pattern of billing and cancellation complaints that its stronger G2 (4.5/5) and Capterra (4.6/5) scores don't fully surface. For a small-to-mid team that wants omnichannel coverage without Intercom's compounding per-resolution math, Crisp is the honest lighter-weight alternative — just read the cancellation fine print first.

Heyy is worth a serious look if what actually drew you to Intercom was Fin's ability to do more than answer FAQs — Heyy's AI Employees carry an attribute-permission system (Read, Share, Update, with Update requiring Read first) that lets an agent capture and write contact data mid-conversation, a more explicit, auditable version of the CRM-context idea Intercom gestures at. Its exit-point system plays a similar role to Intercom's escalation logic but is more configurable in plain language — teams can define distinct outcomes like escalate-to-human, refund-request, or a custom resolution state, each independently wired into automation flows rather than a single generic handoff trigger. On live data specifically, Heyy's documentation explicitly warns against crawling a store platform for prices or stock and instead routes that through Custom API actions with response mapping — a more deliberate design against hallucinated answers than Intercom's own docs describe. Channel coverage is narrower, though: Web Chat, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, and SMS, with no phone/voice channel the way Intercom offers. The honest gap is proportional: Heyy has no publicly documented dollar pricing (plan tiers are gated by AI Employee count, knowledge storage, and actions rather than seats) and no independent review base yet on G2, Capterra, or Trustpilot to check vendor claims against, unlike Intercom's 2,900+ G2 reviews at 4.5/5. Reasonable pick for a team drawn to the CRM read/write model who's willing to run a sales call to get real pricing and accept some platform risk in exchange.
